structural_donor.scope: DEPOT-01 WS and BASE-01 to DEPOT-01 two-hour FAST StationStructure only

manual_basis: Installed manual physical pp338-339 and 439-441 ties task-referenced ItemRepair to matching selected TCID/TLID and STID. An existing E04 FAST accepted model demonstrates this depot WS and two-hour upward/downward transport structure.
controlled_delta: Both arms have the same aircraft, mission schedule, seed and horizon; two ItemRepair rows for the same LRU and task (one hour at BASE-01 and DEPOT-01); base spare1 and depot spare0 under both POINTs; and MaintenanceAllocation AIR_BASIC LRU-CM/BASE to BASE-01 versus AIR_DEPOT LRU-CM/BASE to DEPOT-01. Frozen inputs differ only in Control.APID and ProblemDescription. There are no ItemReorder or ResourceAllocation business rows.

pre_run_hypotheses.common: The same first failed physical LRU should abort the first mission, consume the base spare, and restore system readiness after SURP. This is a hypothesis; if identity or demand diverges, preserve as diagnostic.
pre_run_hypotheses.base: The selected BASE-01 ItemRepair should directly repair failed LRU ID1 at BASE-01, then return it to local stock. A rough target from prior controls is h10.1667-11.1667, subject to native confirmation.
pre_run_hypotheses.depot: The selected DEPOT-01 ItemRepair should cause failed LRU ID1 to move BASE-01 to DEPOT-01 over two hours, repair there for one hour, then return toward BASE-01 over two hours. Rough expected return is h15.1667, subject to native confirmation.
pre_run_hypotheses.alternatives: Duplicate-IID repair rows, station activation, converter, transport, or later stock/mission differences may invalidate the intended contrast. If observed routing or conversion differs, retain a diagnostic, not a positive selection claim. Later stochastic parity is not a required claim.

limits: The bounded claim is APID selection of maintenance repair station for LRU-CM/BASE in this model. It does not isolate downstream transport, stock or later mission differences as separate mechanisms.
